title: Regev: Short-Vector Factoring
statement: Conditional nontrivial-factor algorithm using independent multidimensional quantum samples and lattice postprocessing.

target.description: Composite $n$-bit integer; the main quantum step treats odd inputs with at least two distinct prime factors.

parameters.name: d
parameters.domain: Theorem 1.1 choice, with integer rounding as in the source.

assumptions: Theorem 1.1 assumes a vector in $L\setminus L_0$ of norm $\exp(O(\sqrt n))$ for the chosen small bases. This hypothesis is not replaced by a later paper's modified-base result.

time.note: No total bound is extracted for this coordinate in the checked result.

memory.note: No total classical/quantum memory bound is extracted for this result.

classical_time.note: Classical postprocessing only; not an aggregate quantum/classical runtime.

quantum_calls.note: Independent samples in Theorem 1.1; lattice-dimension rounding is implicit in the source.

gates_per_call.note: Per invocation of the algorithmic circuit, not total gate count or an implementation estimate.

success.description: A constant-success argument is given, but the checked edition conflicts on the lattice-event probability: Corollary 4.5 states at least 1/4, while the theorem proof invokes failure probability 1/4. No numeric primary probability is certified here.

review.scope: Compared Corollary 4.5 and the theorem proof, including sampling errors; the inconsistent probability statements remain unresolved.

evidence.locator: PDF/printed p. 3, Theorem 1.1; pp. 7–8, Corollary 4.5 and proof of Theorem 1.1.
evidence.interpretation: Targeted transcription of this result's input, output, cost accounting and success event; not a full-paper audit.

limitations: Nontrivial factor, not a separately costed recursive complete factorization.
The super-polynomial classical tradeoff mentioned in the introduction is outside this selected configuration.
No numerical frontier comparison; success conflict and symbolic costs remain.

field_conflicts.label: Probability statement mismatch
field_conflicts.description: The corollary's success lower bound and its use in the theorem proof have different numerical meanings. Neither 3/4 nor 1/4 is silently substituted as the complete factoring success probability.

observations.reported: Lattice event has probability at least 1/4.
The same corollary property is invoked with failure probability 1/4.
